title: How the workshop should be remembered and closing thoughts
summary: He wants it remembered as a platform for boundless high-level music and hopes attention will help innovators and make jazz appealing for tourism in the home of jazz.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: How do you want the workshop remembered?

I wanted to be remembered as a place that was definitely dedicated to just playing a high, high form of music that had no boundaries, and that wanted to, even with its freedom, to be as enjoyable as any commercial music that people choose to think is what people would want to do. It's what people want to hear. And as a place that made an attempt to give a platform for players to just be able to play whatever they felt. You know, excuse me.
Okay. Is there anything else that we haven't covered that you want to say about the workshop? I mean, we've talked about quite a few things, but...

Well, not really. I mean, I'm sure that when I leave here, I'll probably say, well, that was something else that I could have said. I just hope that through your efforts of bringing this to people's attention, that maybe they will see reason to start plugging into people who are innovators of the music, and may have some different suggestions as to how to make it more appealing to younger players that might want to pursue a higher form of the music, not for their music to be dictated to and suppressed by record companies that are just looking for some formula to make money. I mean, the idea is to make money, but I still think that this music is worth something. And I mean, it's proven. I mean, when you have opportunities to go to Europe and see the difference in the way people accept the art form, that it's just a matter of education and a matter of, I guess, the powers that be to see that we've tried all of the other ways, and maybe this is another way that we could start exploring, and may tend to increase people's interest in tourism and jazz. I mean, it's just the home of jazz.
